messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for customer 'HavenBridge' - private VPC egress failures observed from their Dedicated pool (pool-d-haven-01). Error spike starts ~T-3m. Alert: 502/503 to external auth API (auth-prod.havenbridge.com)

sam (oncall): seeing same in logs, dozens of concurrent TLS timeouts to auth provider. customer reports login failures.

alison (sre): quick healthcheck - NLB targets for pool-d-haven-01 show 503 unhealthy on `/healthz`. Backend app nodes still up, but health check failing.

lee (network): I'm pulling VPC flow logs now, but initial look: many connections to 3rd-party IPs are RST or timed out. Could be SG or NAT saturation.

mike (platform): last config push at T-15m included sg-egress-hardening for dedicated pools (terraform apply). Rolling back?

jordan (cs-havenbridge): HavenBridge support pinged asking if we see customer-wide login issues. They need ETA for mitigation.

sam (oncall): paging network oncall @lee. Step 1: isolate customer traffic to stop impact spreading. Options: (a) temp allow egress 443 to auth provider via sg, (b) route traffic through shared outbound proxy pool. Thoughts?

lee (network): quick triage - SG change removed 0.0.0.0/0:443 allow for the dedicated pool, replaced with tight CIDR list. Auth provider IPs not in list -> blocked. Also seeing conntrack close spikes on NAT gw at ~T-4m. Likely both: policy block + NAT conntrack exhaustion.

alison (sre): confirm: SG modification came from terraform module `sg-egress-restrict` in `infra/dedicated/pool`. We should revert SG to previous state for pool-d-haven-01 and create scoped exception for provider while we stabilize.

mike (platform): I can do a targeted terraform rollback for that one module. Command I will run:
```bash
cd infra/dedicated/pool
terraform apply -target=module.sg_egress_restrict.module.pool[\"d-haven-01\"] -var-file=prod.tfvars
```
Will run if we agree.

sam (oncall): do it. Meanwhile lee, can you open conntrack headroom? Any quick kernel tuning?

lee (network): on the NAT instances we can temporarily drop conntrack timeout and clear some entries. Running: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` to check. Also can scale NAT throughput by attaching one more NAT ENI in autoscaling group.

alison (sre): I'll coordinate with deploy-bot to create a temporary egress-proxy in the regional shared pool and update route table for the customer's subnets to point to the proxy. That avoids global SG rollbacks if they object.

deploy-bot: started runbook step: create ephemeral egress-proxy instance in us-west-2-shared-pool. ETA ~4m. (logs: task-7821)

jordan (cs-havenbridge): I'll tell HavenBridge: "We have a mitigation plan: ephemeral egress proxy + targeted security group rollback. Expect intermittent improvements in ~6-8 minutes. We'll follow up when fully restored."

sam (oncall): mike - proceed with targeted terraform apply now. Marking as hot rollback.

mike (platform): running apply now. output:
```
Apply complete! Resources: 1 changed, 0 added, 0 destroyed.
Changed security group rules for sg-0a1b2c3d (pool-d-haven-01) - re-added outbound 443 to 3.4.5.0/24 and auth provider ranges.
```

lee (network): sg rule restored. Performing tcp handshake check to auth provider from one of affected nodes:
```
curl -v https://auth.prod.example.com/healthz
* Connected to auth.prod.example.com (3.4.5.22) port 443 (#0)
> GET /healthz HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

alison (sre): NAT conntrack still high. Cleared ~32k stale entries and bumped nf_conntrack_max to 262144. After clearing, observed drop in retransmits.

lee (network): also attached additional NAT capacity (added nat-eni-07) to the AZ. Routing propagation confirmed.

sam (oncall): traffic to auth provider looks back to normal on metrics, 5xxs dropping to baseline. NLB target health flipping to healthy.

deploy-bot: ephemeral egress proxy created and route table update applied to subnets a/b for pool-d-haven-01. Proxy IP: 10.20.30.45.

jordan (cs-havenbridge): customer reports login flow working again. They asked what caused it exactly.

sam (oncall): root cause: recent SG hardening terraform change removed provider IP ranges from dedicated pool outbound whitelist; combined with NAT connection-tracking spike (stale entries) produced a window where most TLS sessions couldn't establish, causing app healthchecks to fail and NLB to mark targets unhealthy.

mike (platform): remediation steps completed: 1) targeted SG rollback for pool-d-haven-01 2) created ephemeral egress proxy and switched route 3) increased conntrack limits + cleared entries 4) added NAT capacity 5) rolling monitor for 30m.

alison (sre): post-mortem actions I want assigned: - pin list of 3rd-party provider CIDRs to infra repo with automated sync - add preflight check in terraform plan that validates outbound CIDRs for dedicated pools - add conntrack alert for >80% usage.

lee (network): I'll add a temporary guardrail in the CD pipeline to block `sg-egress-restrict` from running without approved exceptions for dedicated pools.

mike (platform): I'll run a quick audit to find other dedicated pools that had the same module applied in last 24h and list owners.

sam (oncall): handing off to next oncall - @alison please take incident owner for followups and postmortem. Key details in this thread.

alison (sre): taking it. I'll open an incident ticket and link runbooks + timelines.

jordan (cs-havenbridge): I'll send a formal incident update to HavenBridge: summary, mitigation, ETA for postmortem (EOD today).

sam (oncall): final checks: monitoring shows 200 OK healthchecks for all targets for 10m, 5xx < baseline. Marking incident as resolved for paging. Will keep thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident auto-close timer set to 60m. If any regressions, react to this thread or reopen.
